items.title: Today's lesson
items.content:
A deodorant listing **butane and isobutane**, and a kitchen with **ethanol** (sanitiser) and **ethanoic acid** (vinegar), open the lesson.

Ethene and ethyne separate **saturated** from **unsaturated** hydrocarbons. Four carbons joined two ways give **isomers**; rings complete the picture.

A table of alkanes shows a **homologous series**; the lesson ends with **functional groups** and **naming**.

items.title: You already know
items.content:
• carbon is tetravalent and shows catenation

• drawing ethane and propane: join the carbons first, then fill the other valencies with hydrogen

• molecular mass from atomic masses (C 12 u, H 1 u)

items.title: By the end, you can
items.content:
**1.** Distinguish saturated and unsaturated hydrocarbons; draw chains, branches and rings.

**2.** Draw structural isomers of butane.

**3.** Identify homologous series and their trends.

**4.** Identify functional groups and name simple compounds.

items.text:
**What this shows**

Left: a boy uses a **deodorant spray**; the can's label lists the gases **butane** and **isobutane**.

**Answer to Question 1**

Take guesses. The same atoms can be **joined in different ways** (Part 2).

**What this shows**

Right: a kitchen with a bottle of **vinegar** (ethanoic acid) and **hand sanitiser** (ethanol).

**Answer to Question 2**

Take guesses. 'Eth' means a chain of **two carbon atoms**, and the ending names the **group** that gives each compound its properties (Part 4).

items.text:
**Answer to Question 3**

**No**: each carbon has only **3 bonds**, so one valency is still free. A second bond between the two carbons uses it: a **double bond**, C=C.

**What this shows**

Step 1: join the two carbons. Step 2: put **two hydrogens on each carbon**. The small circles mark valencies still free.

Then reveal steps 1 and 2 (pointer 2 sets them up), and finally step 3: the double bond.

items.text:
**Answer to Question 4**

**Three**: each carbon has one hydrogen, so it needs 3 more bonds, all to the other carbon: a **triple bond**, C≡C.

**What this shows**

Electron-dot structures (top) and structural formulae (bottom) of ethane, ethene and ethyne. × is one carbon's electron, • the other atom's.

**Answer to Question 5**

Ethene: **4** (two shared pairs). Ethyne: **6** (three shared pairs).

items.prompt: The figure shows three hydrocarbons. Which of them are unsaturated?

items.text:
**On this question**

**A**: (i) propane has only single bonds: **saturated**. (ii) propene has a **C=C double bond** and (iii) ethyne a **C≡C triple bond**: both **unsaturated**. With single bonds only, 3 carbons carry 8 hydrogens; $\mathrm{C_{3}H_{6}}$ has 2 fewer, so it needs one double bond.

script.x: Activate the question: the figure is part of it. Explain depending on time available.
Pointer 1 carries the reasoning.

items.text:
**Answer to Question 6**

**Two ways**: a **straight chain** of four, and a chain of three with the fourth carbon joined to the **middle** carbon.

**What this shows**

(a) The two **carbon skeletons** (hydrogens not shown).

**What this shows**

(b) The **complete molecules**: hydrogens fill the other valencies.

**Answer to Question 7**

Both are $\mathrm{C_{4}H_{10}}$: the **same formula**, but the atoms are joined differently.

items.text:
**Answer to Question 8**

Three carbons can be joined in **only one way**. Drawing the chain bent does not make a new compound.

**What this shows**

Propane: three carbons in a chain, hydrogens filling the other valencies.

**What this shows**

Carbon atoms in a **ring**: cyclohexane (skeleton and complete molecule) and benzene.

items.prompt: Which carbon skeleton (hydrogens not shown) is an isomer of butane rather than butane itself?

items.text:
**On this question**

**C**: one carbon is joined to the **middle** carbon of a chain of three. (A), (B) and (D) are a chain of four carbons drawn bent, so each is butane.

items.text:
**What this shows**

The first six alkanes: number of carbons, name, formula, structure and boiling point.

**Answer to Question 9**

Each differs from the next by one $\mathrm{CH_{2}}$ unit, so the mass rises by 12 + 2 × 1 = **14 u**.

**Answer to Question 10**

They **rise steadily** with molecular mass. **Methane to butane** boil below 298 K, so they are gases; **pentane and hexane** are liquids.

Questions 9 and 10. Answers are on pointers 2 and 3.
Show the key idea: homologous series.

items.text:
**What this shows**

The first members of three homologous series: alkanes, alkenes and alkynes.

**Answer to Question 11**

Alkenes: **2n**, so $\mathrm{C_nH_{2n}}$. Alkanes: **2n + 2**, so $\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+2}}$. Alkynes: **2n − 2**, so $\mathrm{C_nH_{2n-2}}$.

script.x: Show the three series. Pointer 1 sets them up.
Question 11. Answer is on pointer 2.
Show the conclusion box.

items.prompt: (i) Write the formula of the next member after $\mathrm{C_{3}H_{7}OH}$ in its series. (ii) Which of $\mathrm{C_{3}H_{8}}$, $\mathrm{C_{4}H_{10}}$ and $\mathrm{C_{5}H_{10}}$ is in the same homologous series as ethene?

items.text:
**On this question**

**A**: (i) add one $\mathrm{CH_{2}}$: $\mathrm{C_{4}H_{9}OH}$. (ii) $\mathrm{C_{5}H_{10}}$ fits $\mathrm{C_nH_{2n}}$ with n = 5; $\mathrm{C_{3}H_{8}}$ and $\mathrm{C_{4}H_{10}}$ are alkanes.

script.x: Activate the question and explain depending on time available. Pointer 1 carries the reasoning.

items.text:
**Step 1: start here**

Read the key idea: a heteroatom replaces a hydrogen, and the group containing it is the **functional group**. Then go to the table (pointer 2).

**What this shows**

**Step 2.** The five functional groups: class, heteroatom, group and how it is written. Reveal in three steps: halo and alcohol; aldehyde and ketone; carboxylic acid.

**Answer to Question 12**

**Step 3**, once aldehyde and ketone are showing.

In an **aldehyde** that carbon is also bonded to a **hydrogen**, so the group sits at the **end** of the chain (—CHO). In a **ketone** it is bonded to two other carbons, so it sits **inside** the chain.

script.x: Pointer 1: show the key idea on heteroatoms and functional groups.

Pointer 3: Question 12, once aldehyde and ketone are showing.

items.text:
**Step 1: start here**

Go through the four naming steps with the class. Then go to the examples (pointer 2).

**What this shows**

**Step 2.** Three-carbon examples: class, prefix or suffix, example. Reveal one group at a time; let students name the compounds first, then reveal the **Name** column beside it.

**Answer to Question 13**

**Step 3**: back to the hook.

Both have a chain of **two carbons** ('eth'). '**-ol**': an alcohol with an **—OH** group, $\mathrm{CH_{3}CH_{2}OH}$. '**-oic acid**': a carboxylic acid with a **—COOH** group, $\mathrm{CH_{3}COOH}$.

items.prompt: Name the three compounds in the figure. Which functional group does (iii) have?

items.text:
**On this question**

**A**: (i) **bromoethane**. (ii) **butanal**: 4 carbons with —CHO at the end. (iii) **butanone**: a **ketone** (C=O inside a chain of 4 carbons).
